findings.title: Signup failure is a separate event and signup has no outcome event to hold status + failure_reason
findings.explanation: signup_form_submitted fires at the start of the handler (intent only). The only outcome signal is signup_form_submit_error, fired from the catch block, so failure lives on its own event (rule 4) and success has no event. 'How many signup attempts fail' needs a union of the two events and can't give a success rate. The catch also skips several end states: the Cloudflare invalid-token error returns silently, as do user-already-exists, checkout-session redirect and account-under-review. These attempts have an intent event and no outcome, so they look like abandonment in a funnel.
findings.fix: Add one outcome event (e.g. signup_completed) with status = success | failed | cancelled and failure_reason (enum). Use values read from the code: user_already_exists, invalid_cloudflare_token, checkout_required, under_review, api_error, sign_in_failed. Do not rename signup_form_submit_error in place. Dual-fire both events for one release (dual_fire_until on the old entry), then mark the old entry deprecated with deprecated_reason and replaced_by. Add a SEMANTICS changelog line. Dashboards on this event's question 'How many signup attempts fail, and why?' move to the new event.
findings.verifier_note: Read `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx` lines 240–335 and searched the repo for any other signup `capture` call (none, apart from the three button clicks). - `signup_form_submitted` fires before the request at :243. The only outcome is `signup_form_submit_error` in the catch at :326, and no event fires on success, so the success rate can't be measured. Several paths end with no outcome event: user already exists (:262–268), the checkout redirect (:271–279), account under review (:285–287) and the Cloudflare invalid-token error (:322–323). They will look like abandonment. Correction for the fix: in `calcomSignupHandler.ts` the checkout case ("Created user but missing payment", :319) and the under-review case (:303) both come after the user has been created. They are not failures, so they should not be `failure_reason` values. Record them as success with a separate dimension, such as `next_step = checkout | under_review`.

findings.title: error_message sends raw free text from the server or client as the failure reason
findings.explanation: error_message is the thrown Error's message. That is result.error.message from the signup API, or a translated UI string. It is unbounded, localized free text, so the same failure splits into many values in a breakdown. Its content is not controlled by the plan, so it could include user-supplied values. The catch also treats an exception from signIn as a signup failure, and the handler doesn't distinguish the two sources.
findings.fix: Replace error_message with a closed failure_reason enum on the new outcome event, mapped from API error codes or the failing step (signup request vs. sign-in). Keep the raw message out of analytics and leave it in the form error and server logs. If you keep a message for debugging, truncate it and mark the values you haven't observed as (UNCONFIRMED).
findings.verifier_note: Read :282, :320 and :331, plus the signup API handlers that produce `result.error.message`. - `error_message` is free text: whatever message the server sends back, a translated fallback, or any error thrown by `signIn`. It is not a closed list. Correction: the text is mostly not localized. The server sends fixed English strings ("Invalid username", "Username or email is already taken", "A user exists with that username", "Signup is disabled", "Internal server error"). The translated `unexpected_error_try_again` text is used only when the thrown value isn't an `Error`. So the breakdown splits less than the finding says. `route.ts:72` passes through an arbitrary `e.message` from `HttpError`, so I can't rule out user-supplied content, but I can't confirm it either. The closed-enum fix still applies, and its values can come from the server strings above.

findings.title: verify_email_already_verified can fire again when feature flags change, and may read onboarding_v3_enabled before flags load
findings.explanation: The event sits in an effect that depends on `[data?.isVerified, flags]`. Once the user is verified, it fires every time the `flags` object changes identity, for example when flags load or refresh. The redirect still runs the first time, but the page can send the event more than once for one visit. If the first run happens before flags are populated, `onboarding_v3_enabled` is undefined and the redirect goes to the wrong path. This inflates the already-verified count and can leave the flag property empty or wrong.
findings.fix: Fire the event once, for example with a ref guard (`hasTracked.current`). Wait until flags are loaded before reading `flags["onboarding-v3"]`. Alternatively, depend only on `data?.isVerified`.
findings.verifier_note: Read `verify-email-view.tsx` lines 46–57, `useFlagMap` (`packages/features/flags/context/provider.ts`) and `useFlags` (`apps/web/modules/feature-flags/hooks/useFlags.ts`). - The flags object is `query.data ?? initialData`. When the tRPC query resolves, `flags` becomes a new object and the effect runs again. A verified user can therefore send the event twice and get two `router.replace` calls, as long as the page is still mounted when the flags arrive. Correction: before the flags load, `flags["onboarding-v3"]` is `false`, not `undefined`, because `initialData` sets it to `false`. So the first event can report `false` when the flag is really on, and the first redirect goes to `/getting-started`; the second run then redirects to the right path. The registry description ("may be undefined if the flags have not loaded") is wrong in the same way and should say "false until flags load". A later refetch that returns the same data probably keeps the same object, because React Query's structural sharing reuses unchanged data, so the "refresh" part of the finding is unlikely in practice.

migration.why: A failure is sent as its own event. Rule 4 puts it on the outcome as status and failure_reason. signup_form_submitted fires before the request, so it is an intent, not an outcome. Add a server-side or post-response outcome event with status = success | failed | cancelled and failure_reason, then deprecate the submit_error event.
error_message sends raw error text (server or client message). Replace it with an enumerated error_reason (for example user_exists | validation | network | unexpected) and stop sending the free text.

The signup intent (signup_form_submitted) has no outcome event for a created account. Add one, sent from the server where the user row is created, so drop-off from submit to account created can be measured.
Intent click with no outcome. Pair with an invite-sent outcome (status, member count after), preferably from the server, to measure drop-off.
Install intent has no outcome event (app installed, with status and failure_reason). Install success is only shown as a toast.
The same call is repeated at three sites (handleAppInstall and two custom onClick wrappers). Extract it into one helper so the properties can't drift apart.

A new onboarding flow (modules/onboarding/getting-started) and the older one (modules/getting-started/[[...step]]) both send onboarding events with different names and shapes. Plan selection and the old step_completed events describe the same funnel. Consider a single onboarding_step_completed with a step property in both flows.
Fires on every radio change and is mostly redundant with onboarding_plan_continue_clicked, which carries the final plan. Only keep it if someone asks about plans considered before continuing.
Dismissing a banner is on the ignore list and answers no stated question; the upgrade click is the event that matters. Candidate for removal unless someone wants the dismissal rate.
The name says insights routing, but SaveFilterSegmentButton is a generic data-table component. Rename, or add a property for the table (for example table_id), and dual-fire if it is on a dashboard.

Sent only from the collapsed-tooltip top-level link and the child link; other render variants of the item may not be tracked. Check that every nav click path calls trackNavigationClick. Also, item_name is a translation key; document that.
It is a click on a navigation item (referral_text, /refer) that navigation_item_clicked can already record. If the click is already tracked there, this is a near-duplicate.

Google and Microsoft are the same action (choosing an SSO provider to sign up) sent as two events. Fold both into one event with a new provider property (google | microsoft). Dual-fire for a window if either is on a dashboard.
Same action as the Google button. Fold into one event with provider = microsoft.

is_org_invite is computed as `orgSlug && !username`, so it is not always a boolean (it can be undefined or an empty string). Wrap it in !! so the type is always boolean. The same expression is used in the other signup events.

The click is an intent event and the outcome comes back through an external OAuth callback. This code does not show a server-side signup outcome event that carries the provider. Without one, drop-off between click and account creation cannot be measured per provider.

A click on resend is intent. The mutation result (success or error) is not tracked, and the success toast shows before the request finishes. Add a status on the outcome, or track it on the server where the email is sent.
The draft types `enabled` as string, but the code sends a boolean from the Switch's onCheckedChange. Set the registry type to boolean.

The draft types it as string, but the code sends a boolean (!!dependency). The Connect button is disabled whenever a dependency is missing, so the value is effectively always false. Consider dropping it, or sending it from the dependency-warning link instead.

Only the outcome is tracked. There is no onboarding start or step event, so drop-off can't be measured (rule 2). The onError path shows a toast but sends nothing. Add an onboarding step event with a `step` property, or add status/failure_reason to this event.

This is an intent event with no outcome. Whether the app got installed is not tracked (install success is handled in onSuccess with only a toast). Add an app-installed outcome event or track it server-side.

The call forwards a free-form Record<string, any> (props.trackingMetadata) as event properties. Nothing in the type stops a caller adding other keys such as user text. Every caller found today sends only section and page. Type trackingMetadata as { section: string; page: string }.

The call uses posthog.capture directly inside a shared UI component instead of a tracking wrapper. The scanner could not read its properties. Check this against the direct_sdk setting in _tracking_profile.yaml.

Finish personal onboarding (continue) on `/onboarding/personal/calendar` (core) has no event: Continue calls updateProfile with completedOnboarding: true, which is the finish line of personal onboarding. `onboarding_completed` is already in the plan, so add these properties and values to it. This shows how many sign-ups finish personal onboarding and whether they connected a calendar first. Add `method`, `has_connected_calendar`, `onboarding_type`.

Save personal profile details and continue onboarding on `/onboarding/personal/profile` (core) has no event: This answers where new users drop off in onboarding. It is a new `step` value and a few properties on the existing event, not a new event. Add `step`, `has_avatar`, `has_bio`, `from_team_onboarding`.

Start connecting a conferencing app via OAuth on `GET /v2/conferencing/:app/oauth/auth-url` (core) has no event. Intent half of the connect flow: how many users start connecting an app (Zoom, Google Meet, Stripe and so on) and which one. The outcome arrives through the OAuth callback, so abandonment is a start with no matching app_connected. Properties: `app_type`, `app`, `api_version`.

Complete conferencing app OAuth connection on `GET /v2/conferencing/:app/oauth/callback` (core) has no event. Outcome of the OAuth connect: how many apps get connected, per app, and how many fail and why. Success and failure share one event through status and failure_reason. Properties: `app_type`, `app`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `is_first_app_connected`, `api_version`.

Look up available slots for an event type on `GET /v2/slots` (core) has no event. Top of the booking funnel: how often a slot lookup returns nothing, and how many lookups turn into a booking. Send counts only, never the user or attendee details. Properties: `api_version`, `result_count`, `has_slots`, `range_days`, `event_type_type`, `entry_point`.

Update an event type on `PATCH /v2/atoms/event-types/:eventTypeId`; Update an event type on `PATCH /v2/event-types/:eventTypeId`; Update an event type on `PATCH /v2/event-types/:eventTypeId` (core) has no event. Answers which event type settings people change after creating one, and how often saving fails. Send field names only, never the values. Properties: `event_type_id`, `changed_fields`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `scheduling_type`, `is_team_event`.

Create a schedule on `POST /v2/atoms/schedules/create`; Create a schedule on `POST /v2/schedules`; Create a schedule on `POST /v2/schedules` (core) has no event. Availability setup is a prerequisite for being bookable, so this answers how many users create their first schedule and how many create extra ones. Properties: `is_first_schedule`, `is_default`, `status`, `failure_reason`.

Send an email verification code on `POST /v2/atoms/verification/email/send-code` (core) has no event. Intent half of email verification: how many codes are requested and how many fail to send. A sent code with no email_verified afterwards is abandonment. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `entry_point`.

Verify an email code on `POST /v2/atoms/verification/email/verify-code` (core) has no event. Outcome of email verification: the share of codes that get verified, and whether failures are wrong code, expired code or rate limit. Use is_authenticated=false for this unauthenticated route. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `is_authenticated`, `attempt_count`.

Exchange authorization code or refresh token for OAuth2 tokens on `POST /v2/auth/oauth2/token` (core) has no event. Shows how many third-party OAuth clients complete authorization, and how many refreshes run versus fail. Grant type separates new authorizations from refreshes. Properties: `grant_type`, `client_id`, `status`, `failure_reason`.

Create a booking on `POST /v2/bookings` (core) has no event. The core outcome of the product: bookings made, by type and API version, and how many fail and why. The intent side is the booker UI, which is recorded on the client. Properties: `booking_type`, `event_type_id`, `api_version`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `is_first_booking`, `requires_confirmation`, `is_seated`, `auth_method`.

Cancel a booking on `POST /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/cancel` (core) has no event. Answers how many bookings are cancelled, by whom and how close to the start time. Never send the cancellation reason text. Properties: `cancelled_by`, `is_recurring`, `cancel_all_remaining`, `is_seated`, `hours_until_start`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `api_version`.

Confirm a booking on `POST /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/confirm` (core) has no event. For event types that require confirmation, this shows how many requests hosts approve and how long they take. Properties: `hours_since_requested`, `status`, `failure_reason`.

Decline a booking on `POST /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/decline` (core) has no event. Pairs with booking_confirmed to give the approval rate for bookings that need confirmation. Send has_reason as a boolean, never the reason text. Properties: `hours_since_requested`, `has_reason`, `status`, `failure_reason`.

Reschedule a booking on `POST /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/reschedule` (core) has no event. Answers how often bookings are moved rather than cancelled, and by whom. It is a different action from creating or cancelling. Properties: `rescheduled_by`, `is_seated`, `hours_until_original_start`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `api_version`.

Create an event type on `POST /v2/event-types`; Create an event type on `POST /v2/event-types` (core) has no event. Answers how many event types API users create each week, and how many are a user's first, which is the first value moment. Send it from the server (`api_version` = 2024_04_15). Properties: `entry_point`, `api_version`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `is_first_event_type`, `length_in_minutes`, `scheduling_type`, `team_id_present`.

Authorize an OAuth client for a user on `POST /v2/oauth/:clientId/authorize` (core) has no event. Answers how many users grant a platform client access, and why they fail. The code shows three failures: client not found, invalid redirect URI, and already authorized. The flow ends in an external callback, so a user who is sent to authorize and never completes it counts as abandonment with no matching event. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `oauth_client_id`.

Create an OAuth client on `POST /v2/oauth-clients` (core) has no event. Answers how many platform customers set up a client each week, and how many are new. This is the first value moment for the platform product, and no existing event covers it. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `permissions_count`, `redirect_uri_count`, `is_first_oauth_client`, `organization_id`.

Create a managed user on `POST /v2/oauth-clients/:clientId/users` (core) has no event. Answers how fast each platform client's user base grows, which is the usage number for the platform product. It's sent from the server because the user is created on a client's behalf. Properties: `oauth_client_id`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `time_zone_set`, `is_first_managed_user`, `user_count_after`.

Reserve a slot on `POST /v2/slots/reservations`; Reserve a slot on `POST /v2/slots/reserve` (core) has no event. Answers how many slot holds turn into bookings, when paired with the booking-created outcome event. It's over the budget of 5 new events, and the reason is that it's the top of the booking funnel. `api_version` = 2024_09_04 here. Properties: `api_version`, `event_type_id`, `reservation_duration_minutes`, `is_authenticated`, `status`, `failure_reason`.

Connect a calendar app on `/onboarding/personal/calendar` (core) has no event. Answers how many new users connect a calendar during onboarding, which calendar, and how many installs fail. Many calendars go through an OAuth redirect, so send it from the server as the outcome, with `entry_point = onboarding_personal`. Install clicks that never reach `app_installed` are abandonment, so an `app_install_started` intent event is worth adding too. Properties: `app_slug`, `app_category`, `entry_point`, `status`, `failure_reason`.

Cancel, confirm, reject or reschedule a booking on `/bookings/[status]` (core) has no event. Answers how many bookings hosts cancel, confirm or reject, and how many of those fail. These are core state changes and should be sent from the server with `status` and `failure_reason`. `action` = cancel | confirm | reject | reschedule, and `cancelled` is not counted as a failure. Create the admin account on `/auth/setup` (core) has no event. Answers how many self-hosted installs get past creating the first admin; one onboarding-step event with a `step` property covers the setup steps. It should be sent from the server, where the user is created. Properties: `step`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `is_first_user`.

Sign in or sign up via NextAuth on `ALL /api/auth/[...nextauth]` (core) has no event. Answers how many people signed in or signed up last week, by method, and how many failed. NextAuth is the one server place every method passes through, so it is the outcome event, and is_new_user marks the sign-ups. Receive an Alby (Lightning) booking payment on `ALL /api/integrations/alby/webhook`; Pay for a booking on `/payment/[uid]` (core) has no event. A booking that starts payment but has no payment_completed counts as abandoned. Properties: `provider`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `booking_id`, `amount_bucket`, `currency`.

Request a password reset email on `/auth/forgot-password`; Request a password reset email on `POST /api/auth/forgot-password` (core) has no event. Answers how often people get locked out and ask for a reset. It is the intent half of a pair with password_reset_completed. Never send the email address. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`.

Set a new password from a reset link on `/auth/forgot-password/[id]`; Reset a password with an emailed token on `POST /api/auth/reset-password` (core) has no event. Answers how many reset requests end in a new password. A request with no completion is an abandoned reset. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`.

Sign in with an identity provider (Google or SAML) on `/auth/login` (core) has no event. Provider sign-in leaves for an external callback, so abandonment is a login_started with no login_completed. This answers how many people start provider login and don't finish. Properties: `method`, `entry_point`.

Authorize an OAuth app to access the account on `/auth/oauth2/authorize` (core) has no event. Answers how many users grant access to third-party apps and how many deny it. Cancelled is the deny button and is not a failure. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `client_id`.

Resend the verification email on `/auth/verify` (core) has no event. Answers how often the verification email doesn't arrive or isn't acted on, which shows verification friction. Properties: `entry_point`, `status`.

Accept or reject a booking from an email link on `GET /api/link` (core) has no event. Hosts of confirmation-required events accept or reject bookings, and the number shows how many pending bookings get resolved, and how, from the email. Fire it on the server in confirmHandler so the dashboard path shares the same event. Accept and reject are one event with `decision`. Exchange an authorization code for an OAuth access token on `POST /api/auth/oauth/token` (core) has no event. Properties: `status`, `failure_reason`, `client_id`, `grant_type`, `uses_pkce`.

Sign up for an account on `POST /api/auth/signup` (core) has no event. Sign-ups are the top of the acquisition funnel, and the server sees both outcomes and failure reasons. Reject a booking with a reason from an email link on `POST /api/verify-booking-token` (core) has no event. Join a video call as a guest on `POST /api/video/guest-session`; Continue to the meeting as a guest on `/video/[uid]`; Sign in to join the meeting on `/video/[uid]` (core) has no event. Connect a calendar on `/settings/my-account/calendars` (core) has no event. Connecting a calendar is the main activation step for a scheduling product. Choose an event type from a user's profile on `/[user]` (core) has no event. Answers how many profile visitors pick an event type, which is the top of the booking funnel by profile. Properties: `entry_point`, `event_type_id`, `is_team_event`, `is_embed`.

Select a date and time on the booker on `/[user]/[type]` (core) has no event. The intent half of booking_created: slots selected against bookings made shows where visitors drop off on the booker. Delete all OAuth client webhooks on `DELETE /v2/oauth-clients/:clientId/webhooks`; Delete an OAuth client webhook on `DELETE /v2/oauth-clients/:clientId/webhooks/:webhookId`; Delete a webhook on `DELETE /v2/webhooks/:webhookId` (secondary) has no event. Delete a schedule on `DELETE /v2/schedules/:scheduleId`; Delete a schedule on `DELETE /v2/schedules/:scheduleId` (secondary) has no event. Remove a selected calendar on `DELETE /v2/selected-calendars` (secondary) has no event. Removing a calendar from conflict checking changes which times appear free. Start connecting a Google or Outlook calendar on `GET /v2/calendars/:calendar/connect` (secondary) has no event. Complete Google or Outlook calendar connection (OAuth callback) on `GET /v2/calendars/:calendar/save` (secondary) has no event. Properties: `calendar_type`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `is_dry_run`.

Start Google Calendar connection on `GET /v2/gcal/oauth/auth-url` (secondary) has no event. Answers how many users start connecting a calendar and how many finish. Update a schedule on `PATCH /v2/atoms/schedules/:scheduleId`; Update a schedule on `PATCH /v2/schedules/:scheduleId`; Update a schedule on `PATCH /v2/schedules/:scheduleId` (secondary) has no event. Update a booking's location on `PATCH /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/location` (secondary) has no event. Changing a location after booking is a different action from rescheduling or cancelling.
